windowTitle: TKE end-to-end closure step 9 - the resource-only Launch access gate refused the application its own install had bound

rootCause.fact: `workspaceLaunchAccessProjectionMismatchFields` compared the Workspace row's `workspaceApiKeyId` against the retained Launch projection unconditionally. A resource-only Launch provisions resources only and therefore carries no key identity on its operation facts, while the default-application installation that follows creates its own Gateway key and writes it onto the same Workspace row in `workspace_application_deployment_driver.go`. The comparison could therefore never agree once the application was installed.
rootCause.consequence: After a real purchase and a completed default-application install, the Workspace entry gate answered 409 `workspace_runtime_truth_unavailable` for both the per-binding origin and the `/w/` path, permanently, even though the Workspace read and the runtime read both reported the application ready. The installed application could not be reached at all.
rootCause.canonicalOwnership: The Launch activation owns the resource entitlement and the Workspace row owns the live application binding and its key identity. The access gate re-derived a key identity the Launch shape does not own, which is the duplicate-writer defect the module contract forbids.

change.shape: The key-identity comparison in `workspaceLaunchAccessProjectionMismatchFields` now applies only to a Launch that actually owns a Gateway key; a `WorkspaceProvisioningResourceOnly` Launch skips it and keeps every other stable projection check. `workspaceLaunchProjectionMismatchFields` (the activation-completion check, a full-Launch path) is unchanged.
change.closedSeam: The public seam is the existing per-binding application origin route, exercised end to end by `TestWorkspaceApplicationOriginServesAfterTheApplicationBindsItsOwnKey`; no new interface, flag, or fallback was added.

red.observed: the application-bound key refused its own ready application: 409 {"error":"workspace_runtime_truth_unavailable"}; the recorded audit was stage=workspace_access reason=canonical_facts_mismatch failed_fields=[workspace_api_key_id]
red.method: the production change was temporarily reverted in the working tree for this run only and restored afterwards

green.covers: the entry now serves the ready application whose own install bound the key, and a full Launch still reports a key-identity disagreement as a defect instead of absorbing it

liveRefusal.workspaceRead: available=true; the customer projection names the install's applicationBinding, and the Gateway budget read resolves keyId 371 from the Workspace row, which is the only writer that can supply it
liveRefusal.runtimeRead: Fabric reports currentApplication.status=ready with the same entryUrl and ready=true, so only the access gate disagreed

claimBoundary: Source-check plus focused owner tests plus a captured live refusal. This proves the Cloud-side defect and its repair at the access-gate owner. It does not prove the refused deployment was fixed in place: the running Candidate 55f4266a predates the repair, so closure requires a new Candidate, an Instance deployment of it, and a separate authorized purchase. It also does not transfer or narrow any Instance obligation recorded under opl-instance-medopl.
notRun: No Candidate was built from this branch and no Instance deployment was dispatched; the protected Instance chain remains the owner of those steps.
No Tencent resource was created, changed, or deleted by this receipt.
No production charge was made; the purchase under step 8 was covered by its own authorization.
